title: Auto-tag generated faces with DSL LHS variable name
description: Today tag_geometry is a manual final step, and mesh_compare_regions reports regions by auto-segmented spatial bins (e.g. spatial_Z-_5) that are opaque to the agent. The DSL parser already knows each assignment's left-hand-side variable name (eye_inset in 'eye_inset = coons_inset_faces(...)'). Thread that name into NodeGraphRuntime so the newly created faces of feature-creating nodes (coons_inset_faces.generated, coons_extrude_mesh.generated, inset_faces, extrude_mesh, and similar) are auto-tagged with the LHS name. Effect: mesh_compare_regions can then report 'eye_inset: p95=0.42, coverage=18%' instead of 'spatial_Z-_5', giving the agent actionable per-feature error signal that lines up with the DSL it just wrote. Surfaced from a live voyage skull run where the worst region was reported as spatial_Z-_5 with no way to map it back to which extrusion caused it.
definition-of-done: 1. NodeGraphRuntime threads the LHS variable name of each assignment into MeshFieldContext (or equivalent) during execution. 2. Feature-creating nodes that expose a 'generated' output (coons_inset_faces, coons_extrude_mesh, inset_faces, extrude_mesh) auto-tag those generated faces with the LHS name at assignment time. 3. Tags accumulate (chaining adds names) and survive the same ops that tag_geometry survives today; destructive ops (coons_patch, subdivide_mesh) still invalidate them, matching current semantics. 4. Subsequent tag_geometry(tags=...) appends to auto-tags rather than overwriting. 5. validate_dsl export writes the LHS tags into the .tags.json sidecar. 6. mesh_compare_regions output includes the LHS-named regions alongside or instead of auto-segmented spatial bins.
testing-plan: 1. Unit test: parse 'x = coons_inset_faces(...)' + 'y = coons_extrude_mesh(generated=x.generated)', run, verify generated faces carry tags ['x'] and ['x','y'] respectively. 2. Integration test on a skull DSL: validate_dsl export .tags.json contains entries for eye_inset, nose_in, brow, maxilla, chin, then mesh_compare_regions report names those regions. 3. Destructive op test: coons_patch after an auto-tagged cage invalidates tags, matching tag_geometry behavior.
